import pandas as pd

# File paths for the source CSV files
source0_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_31/training_0.csv"
source1_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_31/training_1.csv"
source2_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_31/training_2.csv"

# Load source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the first numerical index column
df_movies = pd.read_csv(source0_path, index_col=0)  # Source3_31_0: ['movie_id', 'title', 'genres']
df_users = pd.read_csv(source1_path, index_col=0)   # Source3_31_1: ['user_id', 'gender', 'age', 'occupation', 'zip']
df_ratings = pd.read_csv(source2_path, index_col=0) # Source3_31_2: ['user_id', 'movie_id', 'rating', 'timestamp']

# Step 1: Join ratings with users on 'user_id' to get gender for each rating
df_ratings_users = pd.merge(df_ratings, df_users[['user_id', 'gender']], on='user_id', how='inner')

# Step 2: Join the above result with movies on 'movie_id' to get the movie title
df_full = pd.merge(df_ratings_users, df_movies[['movie_id', 'title']], on='movie_id', how='inner')

# Step 3: Group by 'title' and aggregate average rating separately for gender 'F' and 'M'
# Filter ratings by gender and compute mean rating per title
df_f = df_full[df_full['gender'] == 'F'].groupby('title')['rating'].mean().rename('F')
df_m = df_full[df_full['gender'] == 'M'].groupby('title')['rating'].mean().rename('M')

# Step 4: Combine the two gender-based averages into one DataFrame
df_target = pd.concat([df_f, df_m], axis=1).reset_index()

# Step 5: Ensure the schema matches the target schema: ['title': string, 'F': float, 'M': float]
# The 'title' column is string by default, 'F' and 'M' are floats from mean aggregation

# Step 6: Save the result to the specified output path
output_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_31/target_multisource_cot.csv"
df_target.to_csv(output_path, index=False)

import pandas as pd

# Read source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the first numerical index column
source0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_31/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_31/training_1.csv", index_col=0)
source2 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_31/training_2.csv", index_col=0)

# Join Source2 with Source1 on user_id
join_1 = pd.merge(source2, source1, on="user_id", how="inner")

# Join the above result with Source0 on movie_id
join_2 = pd.merge(join_1, source0, on="movie_id", how="inner")

# Compute mean rating by gender per title
# Pivot table approach: group by title and gender, then unstack gender to columns F and M
pivot = join_2.groupby(['title', 'gender'])['rating'].mean().unstack()

# Rename columns to match target schema: 'F' and 'M'
pivot = pivot.rename(columns={'F': 'F', 'M': 'M'})

# Reset index to have 'title' as a column
result = pivot.reset_index()

# Ensure columns are exactly as target schema
result = result[['title', 'F', 'M']]

# Write to target file
result.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_31/target_multisource_critique_history.csv", index=False)
